note: Both sets capture the core facts correctly — turbine configuration, controller goals and operating ranges, filter type, and the y/u variable definitions — with quotes that support the claims. Set B adds no new facts beyond Set A but restates several of them under different entity names (the two power-production control systems, the generator-torque operating range, the filter type, and the nonpower-production actions), giving it more duplication. Set A is therefore the cleaner and equally complete set, so it is preferred.
remarks: Both sets omit several facts on the page: that generator speed is the sole feedback input for both controllers, that nacelle-yaw control actions were not developed (and why yaw is neglected), and the filter equations (7-1), (7-2), (7-3a) including the coefficient relation alpha = e^(-2*pi*Ts*fc) and the definitions of Ts and fc. Set B's claim on the full-span rotor-collective blade-pitch controller adds a 'power-production operation' condition not present in its quote (it comes from the preceding sentence), a minor over-specification. Set A duplicates the filter-type claim and the nonpower-production claim under two entity names; Set B duplicates four facts.
